scenarios.title: Price pressure may outlast the year
scenarios.projection: The IMF projects global inflation of 4.7% and growth of 3.1% for the whole of 2026.
scenarios.reading: A difficult final stretch for purchasing power is plausible; a global average cannot predict your household bills.
scenarios.stronger: Energy costs stay elevated and inflation broadens.
scenarios.weaker: Supply improves and inflation falls faster than projected.
scenarios.limit: Full-year projection, not a separate forecast for November and December.

scenarios.title: A modest recovery, with little room for shocks
scenarios.projection: The IMF projects 3.4% global growth and 4.1% inflation in 2027, with risks tilted downwards.
scenarios.reading: Gradual relief is a plausible baseline, rather than a return to cheap money everywhere.
scenarios.stronger: Inflation eases while investment holds up.
scenarios.weaker: Conflict, trade barriers or weaker AI investment disrupt the baseline.
scenarios.limit: Countries can diverge sharply from the global forecast.

scenarios.title: The electricity race gathers speed
scenarios.projection: The IEA forecasts electricity demand growth of 3.6% in 2026 and 3.8% in 2027, and renewables overtaking coal generation in 2026.
scenarios.reading: More demand and cleaner supply can arrive together. Connecting that supply becomes a practical bottleneck.
scenarios.stronger: Demand rises while connection delays persist.
scenarios.weaker: Demand slows or grid capacity catches up.
scenarios.limit: Global generation shares do not predict local prices or outages.

scenarios.title: Near-record heat remains the backdrop
scenarios.projection: WMO expects global temperatures near record levels in 2026–2030, with an 86% chance that at least one year exceeds the 2024 record.
scenarios.reading: Planning for recurring heat stress is more grounded than naming the exact year or place of a disaster.
watch: El Niño and La Niña conditions
scenarios.stronger: Observed temperatures track the upper part of the outlook.
scenarios.weaker: Natural variability temporarily moderates annual temperatures.
scenarios.limit: 86% applies to the five-year window, not each year. A single warm year is not the Paris Agreement's long-term threshold.

scenarios.title: The grid could set the pace of the transition
scenarios.projection: The IEA's 2026–2030 outlook projects average annual electricity demand growth of 3.6% and calls for faster grid expansion.
scenarios.reading: By the late 2020s, connection capacity could matter as much as adding generation.
scenarios.stronger: Demand grows faster than usable network capacity.
scenarios.weaker: Grid upgrades and flexibility relieve congestion.
scenarios.limit: A multi-year direction, not an exact forecast for the selected year.

scenarios.title: Half of electricity could come from renewables and nuclear
scenarios.projection: The IEA projects renewables and nuclear together supplying around half of global electricity in 2030.
scenarios.reading: A changing power mix looks plausible; electricity is only part of the energy system.
scenarios.stronger: Clean generation and grid connections grow together.
scenarios.weaker: Construction delays or weaker output slow the shift.
scenarios.limit: This is an electricity projection, not a claim that half of all energy is clean.
